instructional_time_model.denominator_rule: All 180 scheduled daily lesson blocks count toward course instructional time, including MID and FINAL support/assessment weeks.
instructional_time_model.qualifying_inquiry_definition: Minutes count only when students frame/test a question or model, analyze/produce data or design evidence, or construct/revise an evidence-based explanation. Lecture/reading, routine practice, navigation, and protected assessment time do not count.
instructional_time_model.status: PASS — source-planned minimum exceeds target; learner completion time remains a separate runtime/evidence question.

weeks.title: Chemical Safety, Measurement & Evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do chemists protect people and evidence while measuring matter?
weeks.phenomenon: Two measurements disagree even though both were recorded carefully.
weeks.lab: Safety/SDS literacy; balance/volume simulation or supervised measurement; never mix household chemicals.
weeks.concepts: hazard; PPE; SDS; significant figures; uncertainty; dimensional analysis
weeks.quantitative: Significant figures, density, dimensional analysis, percent error, uncertainty.
weeks.reading: Course safety charter and sample SDS excerpts.
weeks.evidence_contract: Trace measurement → units → uncertainty → claim; distinguish hazard evidence from safety rules.
weeks.inquiry_contract: Safety/SDS analysis and supervised or simulated measurement design.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve unit conversion and proportional reasoning; revise a measurement claim when uncertainty changes.

weeks.title: Atomic Models & Evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How did experimental evidence change models of the atom?
weeks.phenomenon: Scattering and emission data could not be explained by earlier atomic models.
weeks.lab: Model-evidence card investigation.
weeks.concepts: proton; neutron; electron; nucleus; model revision
weeks.quantitative: Atomic notation, proton/neutron/electron counts, charge accounting.
weeks.reading: Open chemistry text on atomic models.
weeks.evidence_contract: Compare model predictions with scattering/evidence patterns; distinguish observation from historical model.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve conservation/particle-counting rules; revise atomic models from contradictory evidence.

weeks.title: Isotopes, Mass & Nuclear Composition
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why can atoms of one element have different masses?
weeks.phenomenon: Mass spectra show several peaks for a single element.
weeks.lab: Mass-spectrum data analysis; no radioactive materials.
weeks.concepts: isotope; mass number; atomic mass; abundance; ion
weeks.quantitative: Weighted-average atomic mass, isotope abundance, normalization checks.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Audit mass-spectrum assumptions, abundance normalization, and data lineage.
weeks.inquiry_contract: Mass-spectrum data analysis; no radioactive materials.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve atomic notation; transfer isotope reasoning to unfamiliar abundance datasets.

weeks.title: Electrons, Spectra & Quantized Energy
weeks.essentialQuestion: What evidence supports quantized electron energies?
weeks.phenomenon: Atoms emit characteristic line spectra rather than every possible color.
weeks.lab: Virtual emission-spectrum analysis.
weeks.concepts: energy level; photon; spectrum; electron configuration; valence electron
weeks.quantitative: c=λν, E=hν, unit conversion, graphical/tolerance reasoning.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate raw spectral lines from model inference; compare residuals/tolerance and model limits.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve atomic-model revision; explain how spectra constrain electron-energy models.

weeks.title: Periodic Patterns & Predictive Chemistry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does periodic position help predict properties?
weeks.phenomenon: Element properties recur in patterns across the periodic table.
weeks.lab: Periodic-trend data investigation.
weeks.concepts: period; group; radius; ionization energy; electronegativity; valence
weeks.quantitative: Trend datasets, comparative ratios, graph-based periodic-property reasoning.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Use evidence to distinguish trend from exception; justify predictions with effective nuclear attraction and shielding.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve electron structure; transfer trend reasoning to unfamiliar elements/ions.

weeks.title: Ionic Bonding & Lattices
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do electrostatic interactions produce ionic compounds with characteristic properties?
weeks.phenomenon: Salt crystals are brittle solids that conduct only under certain conditions.
weeks.lab: Conductivity/property dataset or supervised low-voltage test with safe materials.
weeks.concepts: ion; ionic bond; lattice; formula unit; charge balance
weeks.quantitative: Charge balance, formula-unit ratios, lattice/property comparisons.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Connect ionic formulas and lattice models to macroscopic properties; preserve model boundaries.
weeks.inquiry_contract: Ionic model/property investigation or safe simulation.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve periodic trends and ion formation; revise formulas from charge-conservation errors.

weeks.title: Covalent Bonds & Lewis Models
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do electron-sharing models explain molecular composition?
weeks.phenomenon: Different molecules can contain the same elements yet have different structures and properties.
weeks.lab: Molecular model kit or paper Lewis structures.
weeks.concepts: covalent bond; Lewis structure; octet model; bond order; resonance model
weeks.quantitative: Valence-electron accounting, formal charge, Lewis-structure comparison.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Compare Lewis/resonance models and state where octet/formal-charge heuristics fail.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve ionic/covalent distinctions; transfer bonding models to unfamiliar molecules.

weeks.title: Molecular Geometry & Polarity
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does three-dimensional shape influence molecular behavior?
weeks.phenomenon: Molecules with polar bonds can be overall polar or nonpolar.
weeks.lab: VSEPR model-building with safe kits or paper models.
weeks.concepts: electron domain; geometry; polarity; dipole; symmetry
weeks.quantitative: Electron-domain counting, VSEPR geometry, polarity/vector cancellation.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Validate shape/polarity predictions against symmetry and molecular evidence.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve Lewis structures; revise polarity claims when geometry changes.

weeks.title: Metals, Solids & Materials Structure
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does structure at the particle scale explain material properties?
weeks.phenomenon: Copper, glass, graphite, and salt behave very differently under stress and electrical conditions.
weeks.lab: Property comparison and material-selection design challenge.
weeks.concepts: metallic bonding; network solid; crystal; alloy; structure–property
weeks.quantitative: Density/property comparisons, weighted engineering decisions.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Use conductivity, density, structure, and defect evidence to justify material choice.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve bonding/structure; transfer evidence to a new material-selection problem.

weeks.title: Intermolecular Forces
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do substances with similar molecular mass have different boiling points?
weeks.phenomenon: Two molecular liquids evaporate at very different rates.
weeks.lab: Evaporation dataset or supervised water/alcohol-free safe simulation.
weeks.concepts: dispersion; dipole-dipole; hydrogen bonding; IMF
weeks.quantitative: Boiling/vapor-pressure trends, comparative IMF reasoning.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate molecular structure, IMF model, and bulk-property observation.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve polarity; revise claims that confuse bond strength with intermolecular force.

weeks.title: Gases & Particle Motion
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can macroscopic gas behavior emerge from particle motion?
weeks.phenomenon: A sealed flexible container changes volume when temperature or pressure changes.
weeks.lab: Syringe simulation with no sealed heating; virtual gas law lab.
weeks.concepts: pressure; temperature; volume; mole; kinetic molecular theory
weeks.quantitative: Boyle/Charles/Avogadro relationships, PV=nRT, transformed graphs, unit-compatible R.
weeks.reading: Open gas-law text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Use graph shape, controls, and residuals to test gas models; distinguish ideal from real behavior.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve particle-motion model; transfer dimensional analysis to gas systems.

weeks.title: Solutions & Concentration
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does particle-level interaction control dissolving and concentration?
weeks.phenomenon: The same mass of solute produces different concentrations in different volumes.
weeks.lab: Safe salt/sugar solution calculation or virtual lab; no tasting.
weeks.concepts: solute; solvent; molarity; dilution; solubility
weeks.quantitative: Molarity, dilution, serial dilution, reverse preparation planning.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Audit meniscus, calibration, transfer, and precision/accuracy evidence.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve mole/volume reasoning; correct dilution plans from conservation-of-solute errors.

weeks.title: Mixtures, Separation & Spectroscopic Evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can chemists separate and identify components of mixtures?
weeks.phenomenon: A colored mixture separates into distinct bands or signals.
weeks.lab: Paper chromatography with washable ink/water or virtual spectroscopy.
weeks.concepts: mixture; chromatography; spectrum; calibration; retention
weeks.quantitative: Recovery, purity, mass balance, Rf, calibration curves, interpolation/extrapolation.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate raw signal, processed measurement, calibration model, and claim; use blanks/standards/duplicates.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve solution concentration; transfer analytical-evidence logic to unknown samples.

weeks.title: Reaction Evidence & Chemical Equations
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do we represent chemical change while conserving atoms?
weeks.phenomenon: Mass appears to change in an open reaction but is conserved in a closed-system model.
weeks.lab: Closed-system simulation or safe effervescent tablet dataset; no sealed pressure build-up.
weeks.concepts: reactant; product; coefficient; state symbol; conservation
weeks.quantitative: Balanced equations, coefficient ratios, atom/mass conservation.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Distinguish reaction evidence from symbolic representation; use conservation as the governing check.
weeks.inquiry_contract: Reaction-evidence studio with safe supplied-data alternatives.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve particle/accounting rules; revise equations by conservation rather than visual balancing alone.

weeks.title: The Mole & Stoichiometry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do chemists count enormous numbers of particles by mass?
weeks.phenomenon: Small measured masses represent astronomical particle counts.
weeks.lab: Mass-to-mole paper/simulation practice.
weeks.concepts: mole; Avogadro constant; molar mass; stoichiometric ratio
weeks.quantitative: Moles, molar mass, mole ratios, mass↔mole and mass↔mass stoichiometry.
weeks.reading: Open stoichiometry text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Audit dimensional-analysis pathways and conservation/reasonableness.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve balanced equations; transfer coefficient meaning to quantitative conversion chains.

weeks.title: Limiting Reactants & Yield
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why does one reactant often determine how much product can form?
weeks.phenomenon: A recipe model stops producing product when one component runs out.
weeks.lab: Paper-token limiting-reactant model.
weeks.concepts: limiting reactant; excess; theoretical yield; actual yield; percent yield
weeks.quantitative: Limiting reactant, theoretical/actual yield, percent yield, boundary sensitivity.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Compare common-product pathways, diagnose >100% yield, separate random/systematic causes.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve stoichiometry; revise limiting-reactant claims when near-stoichiometric uncertainty matters.

weeks.title: Redox & Solution Stoichiometry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can electron transfer and solution measurements quantify reactions?
weeks.phenomenon: Some reactions transfer electrons and produce measurable electrical or color changes.
weeks.lab: Redox-number analysis and virtual/supervised solution stoichiometry.
weeks.concepts: oxidation; reduction; oxidation number; titration concept; equivalence
weeks.quantitative: Oxidation numbers, electron accounting, n=MV solution stoichiometry, equivalence ratios.
weeks.reading: Open redox and solution-stoichiometry text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate formal oxidation-state bookkeeping from observed solution evidence; preserve charge/atom conservation.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve stoichiometry and ions; transfer electron/accounting logic to coupled redox problems.

weeks.title: Midterm Examination & Corrections
weeks.essentialQuestion: What have I mastered about atomic structure, bonding, properties, and stoichiometry?
weeks.phenomenon: A cumulative unknown requires structure–property and quantitative reasoning.
weeks.lab: No new wet lab; midterm and correction portfolio.
weeks.concepts: cumulative synthesis
weeks.quantitative: Mixed semester quantitative retrieval across Weeks 01–17.
weeks.reading: Review notebook and lab evidence.
weeks.evidence_contract: Use readiness evidence, correction classification, and portfolio traceability without exposing protected MID content.
weeks.inquiry_contract: Public practice/portfolio audit only; supervised MID authority remains separate.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Repair prerequisite chains, then verify transfer with new public practice items.

inquiry_minutes_plan.classification: assessment/support week; zero new inquiry minutes counted

weeks.title: Reaction Rates & Rate Data
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can reaction progress be measured mathematically?
weeks.phenomenon: Concentration changes nonlinearly with time during a reaction.
weeks.lab: Rate-curve data analysis.
weeks.concepts: rate; concentration; time; slope; rate law concept
weeks.quantitative: Average/instantaneous rate, tangent slopes, initial-rate ratios, empirical order inference.
weeks.reading: Open kinetics text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate raw measurements, calculated rates, fits, and mechanism claims; track timing/mixing uncertainty.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve concentration, stoichiometry, and graph reasoning; revise rate-law claims from controlled comparisons.

weeks.title: Collision Theory & Conditions
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do temperature and concentration affect reaction rate?
weeks.phenomenon: A reaction speeds up as particles collide more frequently or energetically.
weeks.lab: Safe simulation/data analysis; no unsupervised reactive mixtures.
weeks.concepts: collision; activation energy; temperature; concentration; surface area
weeks.quantitative: Rate ratios under temperature/concentration/surface-area changes.
weeks.reading: Open collision-theory text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Use collision frequency, energy distribution, and effective-collision fraction without overgeneralizing.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve kinetic-temperature and concentration models; transfer collision theory to new rate scenarios.

weeks.title: Mechanisms & Catalysts
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can a multi-step pathway control overall reaction rate?
weeks.phenomenon: A catalyst changes reaction rate without changing overall reactants/products.
weeks.lab: Energy-profile/model analysis.
weeks.concepts: mechanism; elementary step; intermediate; catalyst; transition state
weeks.quantitative: Mechanism step summation, rate-law compatibility, energy-profile comparison.
weeks.reading: Open kinetics mechanisms overview.
weeks.evidence_contract: Test mechanisms against net stoichiometry, empirical rate law, intermediates, and catalyst behavior.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve rate laws; revise mechanism claims when one evidence category fails.

weeks.title: Kinetics Inquiry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can evidence distinguish competing explanations of reaction rate?
weeks.phenomenon: Two rate datasets can fit different models until an additional variable is tested.
weeks.lab: Guided inquiry using simulation or teacher-supervised safe reaction.
weeks.concepts: hypothesis; variable; rate model; residual; uncertainty
weeks.quantitative: Replicate rate metrics, model predictions, residuals, controlled-variable analysis.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Use falsifiable competing models, residual structure, controls, and contrary evidence.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve Weeks 19–21; transfer model-discrimination logic to unfamiliar kinetics data.

weeks.title: Thermochemistry & Calorimetry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can heat transfer reveal reaction-energy change?
weeks.phenomenon: A process warms or cools its surroundings by a measurable amount.
weeks.lab: Virtual calorimetry or teacher-supervised water-based calorimetry.
weeks.concepts: system; surroundings; heat; enthalpy; calorimeter
weeks.quantitative: q=mcΔT, calorimeter heat capacity, qsystem≈−qsurroundings, molar ΔH.
weeks.reading: Open thermochemistry text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Trace raw mass/temperature → q → reaction heat → molar enthalpy; diagnose heat-loss bias.
weeks.inquiry_contract: Calorimetry investigation or safe data alternative.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve energy conservation and units; revise sign/scaling errors with independent checks.

weeks.title: Bond Energy & Hess's Law
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can energy changes be combined across reaction pathways?
weeks.phenomenon: Different reaction sequences can produce the same overall chemical change.
weeks.lab: Hess-cycle card model and bond-energy calculation.
weeks.concepts: bond energy; Hess's law; state function; pathway
weeks.quantitative: Bond-energy estimates, Hess reversal/scaling/cancellation, state labels, uncertainty accumulation.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Compare bond-energy, Hess, and calorimetry pathways; preserve thermodynamic states and input uncertainty.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve enthalpy scaling; transfer state-function reasoning to alternate pathways.

weeks.title: Energy, Entropy & Direction
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do some energetically possible changes occur more readily than others?
weeks.phenomenon: Some processes spread matter or energy even when they absorb heat.
weeks.lab: Particle-distribution simulation.
weeks.concepts: entropy; dispersal; microstate concept; spontaneity
weeks.quantitative: ΔG=ΔH−TΔS, unit conversion, crossover temperature, microstate/probability models.
weeks.reading: Open introduction to entropy.
weeks.evidence_contract: Replace 'disorder' slogans with dispersal/multiplicity evidence; separate thermodynamics from kinetics.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve thermochemistry; revise direction claims using ΔH, ΔS, T, and model limits.

weeks.title: Dynamic Equilibrium & K
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can forward and reverse processes continue while concentrations remain stable?
weeks.phenomenon: A system reaches stable concentrations even though microscopic reactions continue.
weeks.lab: Equilibrium simulation.
weeks.concepts: dynamic equilibrium; equilibrium constant; reaction quotient concept
weeks.quantitative: K expressions and transformations, Q vs K, dynamic rate/concentration graphs.
weeks.reading: Open equilibrium text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate equal rates from equal concentrations; distinguish composition tendency from speed.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve kinetics and thermodynamics; predict direction from Q/K rather than slogans.

weeks.title: Le Châtelier & System Response
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does an equilibrium system respond to disturbance?
weeks.phenomenon: Changing concentration or temperature shifts the observed composition of a reversible system.
weeks.lab: Virtual equilibrium perturbation lab.
weeks.concepts: stress; shift; equilibrium position; temperature; concentration
weeks.quantitative: Q/K response to concentration, volume/partial-pressure, inert-gas, and temperature changes.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate instantaneous disturbance from later reaction response; identify whether Q, K, both, or only rates change.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve Week 26; revise Le Châtelier explanations through explicit equilibrium-expression reasoning.

weeks.title: Solubility & Coupled Equilibria
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do some salts dissolve only slightly, and how can conditions alter solubility?
weeks.phenomenon: A small concentration change can trigger precipitation.
weeks.lab: Solubility-curve/data analysis; no unsupervised precipitation chemistry.
weeks.concepts: solubility; saturation; precipitation; Ksp concept; common-ion concept
weeks.quantitative: Molar solubility, Ksp, Qsp, stoichiometric s relationships, post-mixing concentrations, precipitation thresholds.
weeks.reading: Open solubility-equilibrium text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate Ksp, solubility, Qsp, and observed precipitation; preserve temperature, ionic background, units, and detection limits.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve equilibrium expressions and solution concentration; transfer Q/K logic to coupled solubility systems.

weeks.title: Acids, Bases & Molecular Models
weeks.essentialQuestion: What do competing acid–base models explain?
weeks.phenomenon: Different substances change indicator behavior in repeatable ways.
weeks.lab: Use virtual indicators or teacher-supervised food-safe indicator only; never mix cleaners.
weeks.concepts: acid; base; proton donor/acceptor; conjugate pair; amphoteric
weeks.quantitative: Conjugate-pair bookkeeping, qualitative strength/equilibrium comparisons, indicator-range bracketing.
weeks.reading: Open acid–base text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Compare Arrhenius and Brønsted–Lowry scope; separate model classification from direct indicator/conductivity evidence.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve equilibrium and water behavior; revise acid/base claims based on formula appearance alone.

weeks.title: pH & Titration Reasoning
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can logarithmic scales and stoichiometry quantify acidity?
weeks.phenomenon: A tiny change in hydrogen-ion concentration produces a large pH shift.
weeks.lab: Virtual titration; supervised neutralization only in equipped lab.
weeks.concepts: pH; pOH; strong/weak; equivalence; indicator
weeks.quantitative: pH=−log[H3O+], inverse logs, pOH/Kw, strong-species stoichiometry, n=MV titration calculations.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate strength, concentration, pH, equivalence, and endpoint; audit logarithm and mole-ratio errors.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve solution stoichiometry and logs; transfer model selection across titration regions.

weeks.title: Buffers & Chemical Regulation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do buffer systems resist changes in pH?
weeks.phenomenon: Adding the same amount of acid changes pure water and a buffer differently.
weeks.lab: Buffer simulation; no biological/medical dosing contexts.
weeks.concepts: buffer; conjugate pair; capacity; equilibrium; regulation
weeks.quantitative: Henderson–Hasselbalch, half-equivalence/pKa, buffer stoichiometry, ratio vs total concentration, capacity.
weeks.reading: Open buffer-system text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate pH prediction from capacity prediction; use stoichiometry before equilibrium after strong-acid/base challenge.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve conjugate pairs and titration curves; design and stress-test a buffer near target pH.

weeks.title: Free Energy & Chemical Driving Forces
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do energy and entropy combine to predict chemical direction?
weeks.phenomenon: A process can be spontaneous even when it absorbs heat.
weeks.lab: Free-energy graph/data analysis.
weeks.concepts: Gibbs free energy; enthalpy; entropy; spontaneity; coupling
weeks.quantitative: ΔG vs ΔG°, ΔG=ΔH−TΔS, crossover T, ΔG°=−RT lnK, conceptual ΔG=ΔG°+RT lnQ.
weeks.reading: Open thermodynamics introduction.
weeks.evidence_contract: Cross-check free-energy direction through thermodynamic and equilibrium routes; preserve standard vs actual-state conditions.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve entropy/equilibrium; revise sign/unit/state errors and validate physical coupling.

weeks.title: Electrochemistry & Energy Conversion
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do redox reactions convert chemical and electrical energy?
weeks.phenomenon: Separated redox processes can drive electron flow through a circuit.
weeks.lab: Virtual galvanic-cell investigation or teacher-supervised low-risk cell.
weeks.concepts: anode; cathode; cell potential; oxidation; reduction
weeks.quantitative: Half-reaction balancing, E°cell=E°cathode−E°anode, ΔG°=−nFE°, voltage/current/energy/power distinctions.
weeks.reading: Open electrochemistry text.
weeks.evidence_contract: Connect redox bookkeeping, measured polarity, standard potential, and real-device limitations; keep electrons out of salt bridge.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve redox and free energy; transfer electron-flow/potential reasoning to unfamiliar cells.

weeks.title: Nuclear Chemistry, Materials & Environmental Chemistry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do nuclear changes differ from chemical changes, and how do materials affect society?
weeks.phenomenon: Radioactive decay changes nuclei while ordinary chemical reactions do not.
weeks.lab: Half-life simulation with coins; no radioactive sources.
weeks.concepts: isotope; decay; fission; fusion; polymer/material; lifecycle
weeks.quantitative: Nuclear equation conservation, exponential half-life, decay timelines, mass-energy reasoning.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Separate nuclear from chemical change; compare fission/fusion and lifecycle evidence; distinguish hazard from risk.
weeks.inquiry_contract: Decay/lifecycle data investigation; no radioactive materials.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve isotopes and energy; transfer exponential and evidence-matrix reasoning to materials/environmental decisions.

weeks.title: Materials Science & Sustainable Chemistry Capstone
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can chemical principles guide a safer, more sustainable material or process?
weeks.phenomenon: A product must meet performance, cost, safety, and environmental constraints.
weeks.lab: Design/evaluate material or process using data; no synthesis of hazardous substances.
weeks.concepts: green chemistry; lifecycle; criterion; constraint; tradeoff; evidence
weeks.quantitative: Functional-unit metrics, normalized decision scores, weighted matrices, sensitivity analysis, evidence ranges.
weeks.reading: Read Tuesday's linked Deep Lesson for this week; study its worked model, vocabulary, evidence limits, and any referenced internal dataset or diagram. Record a one-sentence synthesis in the evidence notebook. The lesson page is the required reading; no external textbook is needed.
weeks.evidence_contract: Trace source → calculation → criterion → recommendation; separate measured evidence from stakeholder weighting.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Retrieve models across the course; stress-test recommendations under changed constraints and uncertain inputs.

weeks.title: Comprehensive Final & Laboratory Portfolio Defense
weeks.essentialQuestion: Can I integrate structure, reactions, energy, kinetics, equilibrium, and quantitative chemistry?
weeks.phenomenon: A multi-part industrial/environmental case requires several chemistry models.
weeks.lab: No new wet lab; cumulative final and portfolio defense.
weeks.concepts: cumulative synthesis
weeks.quantitative: Mixed cross-unit quantitative retrieval and model selection; no protected-final item reproduction.
weeks.reading: Complete course portfolio.
weeks.evidence_contract: Map readiness, portfolio traceability, correction-transfer evidence, and course-defense claims while preserving final-exam authority.
weeks.inquiry_contract: No new wet lab; public practice, portfolio audit, and supervised-final support only.
weeks.retrieval_contract: Repair earliest prerequisite weaknesses and verify transfer with new public examples.

assessment.unit: Performance task: model + data/quantitative reasoning + CER + application/design
assessment.midterm: 15-item cumulative objective check plus corrections and portfolio review
assessment.final: 30-item cumulative objective check plus portfolio/capstone defense

safety.lab_policy: Target ≥25% inquiry/laboratory time. Hazardous chemistry requires appropriately equipped, educator-supervised laboratory conditions; home learners use safe simulations/data alternatives.
safety.home_rule: Use only explicitly safe investigations; substitute simulation/data analysis whenever proper supervision or facilities are unavailable.

prior_year_retrieval.correction_requirement: identify inherited concept/practice, current application, error type, corrected reasoning, and one changed-context transfer check
prior_year_retrieval.protected_assessment_boundary: confidential or supervised evidence may satisfy inherited retrieval; protected items/keys must not be exposed in the public repository
